# Screw Boss Lead-In

Screw bosses whose hole has no chamfer or countersink to start the screw.

<figure markdown="span">
![Screw Boss Lead-In: on the left what to avoid, on the right what to aim for](../../assets/diagrams/boss-hole-lead-in-light.svg#only-light){ width="640" }
![Screw Boss Lead-In: on the left what to avoid, on the right what to aim for](../../assets/diagrams/boss-hole-lead-in-dark.svg#only-dark){ width="640" }
<figcaption>A chamfer or countersink at the top of a screw boss's hole, to start the screw straight.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Where it applies

| Process | Criticality |
| :-- | :-- |
| [Plastic Injection Molding](../../reference/processes/plastic-injection-molding.md) | Low |

## Values

This rule has no number to meet: when it finds the problem, it reports it as the error or warning set here.

Criticality in this process: **Low** ([what this means](../../concepts/criticality.md)).

| Material | If detected | Source |
| :-- | :-- | :-- |
| **Default** | Warning | Not yet sourced |

Every other material uses the Default values: PLA, ABS, Acetal / POM, PMMA, LCP, Long-Fiber Reinforced Plastics, PA, PC, PET / PBT, PE, PSU, PP, PS, PUR, PVC.

## Messages

What the results panel says about a finding. You can rewrite these in the Process Library; the words in `{braces}` are filled in for each finding.

!!! warning "Warning"

    No Lead-In on Screw Boss: the hole in `{feature}` (`{size}`) starts square. Without a chamfer or countersink the screw is hard to start straight, and its first thread can crack the top of the boss. Add a small chamfer, about 0.3 to 0.5 mm, at the top of the hole.
!!! failure "Error"

    No Lead-In on Screw Boss: the hole in `{feature}` (`{size}`) starts square. Without a chamfer or countersink the screw is hard to start straight, and its first thread can crack the top of the boss. Add a small chamfer, about 0.3 to 0.5 mm, at the top of the hole.
| Placeholder | Replaced with |
| :-- | :-- |
| `{feature}` | What it is about, such as "Boss 3 (screw)" or "Face12" |
| `{size}` | Its size or what was found, such as "Ø3.00 mm and 9.00 mm deep" |
